subject: Capacity request & lockstep prioritization for Aurora AI launch
messages:
From: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@auroraai.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Aurora AI Sales <sales@auroraai.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity for Q3 product launch — Aurora AI

Markus,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're on a tight timeline: Aurora plans to launch the real-time summarization feature on June 1 and we expect a high concurrency window for the first 8 weeks. Below are the provisional numbers from our traffic sims:

- 95th percentile concurrent requests: ~1,200
- Expected avg tokens per request: 320
- Peak sustained token throughput (24h): ~900M tokens/day
- Target model: open-llama-70B-opt (we can consider quantized variants)

We need clarity on whether Redwood can provide a dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) for this workload with an SLA for latency and a committed throughput starting May 1. If reserved capacity is not fully available, we need to understand the prioritization policy and mitigation options (burst, fallback to smaller model, queueing).

Can you confirm next steps and whether we should expect a firm commit by early April? I've attached our request brief (RDW_Aurora_capacity_request.pdf).

Appreciate a quick turnaround — launch date is firm.

Best,
Eleanor Park
Product Ops Lead, Aurora AI
E: eleanor.park@auroraai.com
T: +1 415 555 0123
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>

Eleanor — thanks for the brief and the clear numbers. We're prioritizing this internally given the launch date. Quick notes:

- We can scope a Dedicated pool, but exact sizing depends on model variant (quant vs fp16) and acceptable tail-latency SLOs.
- We have competing commitments across other Q2 deals; I want to loop in Capacity/Product for a decision matrix so we can provide a firm yes/no by 04/05.

Karthik, Laura — can you review the attached request and propose a recommended allocation (reserve % + burst plan) and list tradeoffs? Please include whether a smaller quantized variant would materially reduce reserve needs and what fallback path (model degrade or queueing) we'll offer Aurora.

Eleanor — I'll coordinate and get back with a proposed commitment and mitigation plan within the week. If helpful, let's pencil a 30m call tomorrow to run through options.

Thanks,

Markus Klein

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 11:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity for Q3 product launch — Aurora AI

Markus — reviewed the brief and ran a quick sizing exercise. Attaching an initial allocation matrix (allocation_matrix_v1.xlsx) — TL;DR below.

Quoted for context: 
> "We need clarity on whether Redwood can provide a dedicated pool (reserved GPUs) for this workload with an SLA for latency and a committed throughput starting May 1."

Options and tradeoffs:

1) Option A — Heavy Reserve (High confidence)
   - Reserve: 120 A100-80GB equiv GPUs (data-modeling -> fp16 equivalent)
   - Cost: High (committed monthly cost + setup)
   - Pros: Headroom for spikes, predictable latency, simple SLA mapping
   - Cons: Reduces pool available for other committed deals; long lead time to firm up hardware allocation

2) Option B — Hybrid Reserve + Burst (Balanced) [Recommended]
   - Reserve: 72 GPUs reserved starting May 1
   - Burst: Additional up to 48 GPUs via burst pool and preemptible capacity for first 8 weeks
   - Fallback: Automated model degrade to quantized 70B variant during sustained >90th pct load; queueing gating for non-priority traffic
   - Pros: Balances cost and availability; gives Aurora a clear SLA for reserved portion while offering elastic headroom
   - Cons: Burst performance variability; requires explicit orchestration and playbooks for failover

3) Option C — Minimal Reserve + Strong Fallback (Conservative)
   - Reserve: 32 GPUs + guaranteed token throughput from cache/cdn optimizations
   - Pros: Low impact to other deals, low cost
   - Cons: Higher risk of latency spikes and degraded UX during peak windows

My recommendation is Option B. Operational notes: we need sign-off from Sales/Revenue (Markus), Capacity (Ben/Laura), and Product (me) by Friday 04/05 to lock the reserve. If we commit Option B, we should also agree on a short-term playbook: model degrade threshold, burst budget, and an SLA addendum for 'best-effort burst'.

Attachments: allocation_matrix_v1.xlsx (detailed GPU-hours, cost delta, expected tail-latencies)

Karthik
Sr. Product Manager, Serving & Capacity
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Eleanor Park <eleanor.park@auroraai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Mar 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Capacity for Q3 product launch — Aurora AI

Eleanor — thanks for the patience while we scoped internally. We converged on the hybrid path (Option B) as the best balance between predictability and cost. Summary of the commitment and next steps:

- Commitment: Reserve 72 A100-80GB equiv GPUs for Aurora starting 2028-05-01 with a 6-month minimum term.
- Burst: Access to up to 48 additional GPUs from burst pools/preemptible nodes for the initial 8-week high-concurrency window; burst is best-effort and comes with an agreed burst budget (see term sheet).
- Mitigation: Automated model degrade to quantized 70B variant above sustained 90th percentile load, plus queue gating for non-priority requests.
- SLAs: Reserved pool will have latency SLOs mapped in the term sheet; burst is explicitly best-effort (we'll publish expected variability).

Action items:
1) Eleanor: please confirm acceptance of the hybrid plan by 03/28 so legal can prepare the term sheet.
2) Laura/Ben: please prepare the placement runbook (node placement, capacity reservation ticket) and list any lead times for procurement.
3) Karthik: finalize the allocation_matrix_v1 -> v2 with actual cost numbers and model degradation thresholds.

I attached the draft term sheet (aurora_commit_term_sheet.pdf) and the allocation matrix. I'll open the HubSpot deal (HS-1342) and push the DocuSign link once we have Aurora's confirmation. If Aurora needs faster ramp, we can discuss a short pilot in April with reduced reserve and a higher burst multiplier.

Markus Klein
Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
